To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a mutation in an intron of the DMD gene can cause Becker muscular dystrophy by activating a cryptic splice donor site.

we identified a novel splice mutation (c.3602+3A>T) causing Becker muscular dystrophy in a patient with dystrophin gene analysis revealing no mutation in the coding region, and we determined that the splice mutation reduced the efficiency and activated a cryptic donor splice site.

a novel mutation in intron 24 of the DMD gene, causing Becker muscular dystrophy, reduced the efficiency of a donor splice site and resulted in activation of a cryptogenic donor site, producing a truncated dystropin protein and a milder Becker phenotype.
